messages:
rekha: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel flip I see p99 spikes on short prompts (<=64 tokens). Looks correlated with batcher creating mixed decode-rate batches. :thinking_face:

jon: can you paste the trace? is this on prod or a dedicated pool?

rekha: prod, cluster eu-west-1, dedicated small-g5 pool. quick trace snippet (span ids trimmed):
```
2024-06-23T15:03:11Z batcher: formed batch size=8 tokens=312 decode_pred_rate=78 tok/s kernels=flash_attn fastpath
2024-06-23T15:03:11Z runtime: selected kernel=kv-quant-16b-flash at 11ms
2024-06-23T15:03:11Z runtime: fallback to slow-kernel after queuing jitter -> extra 24ms
2024-06-23T15:03:11Z decode: tail latency p99=152ms (baseline ~110ms)
```

maya: ugh. that 'queued jitter' line looks like the admission policy is allowing a slow request into a hot microbatch. Do we still use decode-rate bucketing to avoid these mixes?

sam: we do, but the classifier's thresholds were relaxed last week to increase throughput. I pushed a probe patch: `batcher.classify.decode_rate_buckets=[30,60,90,150]` -> previously was `[20,50,100,200]`. Might be wider bins now so 78 tok/s got grouped with 30-90 bin and ended up in same pool as much slower 35 tok/s requests.

rekha: that could explain it. Also noticed KV prefetch budgets dipping on these mixed batches (prefetch misses higher). profiler shows increased KV misses for short prompts in mixed batches.

profiling-bot: perf-profile (excerpt) for request id d4f2:
```
cpu: 12% -> kernel switch overhead 0.9ms
gpu_kv_cache_misses: short_prompts_mixed_batch = 18/80 (22%)
gpu_kv_cache_misses: short_prompts_homogeneous = 4/48 (8%)
decode_step_time: mixed=1.8ms/step homogeneous=1.5ms/step
```

jon: 22% KV miss is significant. Misses amplify when we pick a kernel that expects hot kv layout. If the batch mixes cold and hot contexts we get extra memcpy/evict churn.

maya: action items? roll kernel flip back? tighten classifier? tweak token budget?

sam: my thought: don't rollback kernel flip yet. Instead: 1) re-run classifier with finer decode-rate buckets around 60-90 tok/s (split 60-75 and 76-90); 2) add a soft token-budget penalty for batches where predicted kv_miss_rate > 15% to avoid mixing; 3) add a short-term probation period after kernel flip where batcher prefers same-kernel coalescing.

rekha: I like (1) + (2). Example config patch to test in staging: 
```yaml
batcher:
  classify:
    decode_rate_buckets: [20,50,60,75,90,150]
  admission:
    token_budget_target: 1200  # was 1500
    kv_miss_soft_limit: 0.15
    kv_miss_penalty_ms: 8
  coalesce_policy:
    prefer_same_kernel_duration_s: 60
```

jon: test matrix: run synthetic traces for short/long prompt mixes, and a replay of 12h of prod traffic with kernel flip ON/OFF. I'll spin that up.

profiling-bot: queued job #4821: replay 12h prod -> expected ~6h runtime.

maya: also add a perf regression check in the rollout job: if p99 for short_prompts rises >10% vs baseline, abort. We need that automated before we flip kernels globally.

sam: noted. I'll also output a debug tag on mixed batches so we can find examples quickly: `X-BATCH-MIXED=1` in trace metadata.

rekha: thanks. If tests look good, let's land the classifier split and token-budget tweak behind a feature flag and run in canary for 1% traffic. @deploy-bot can you schedule canary deploy when replay passes?

deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy to eu-west-1 1% at 2024-06-24T02:00:00Z if job #4821 succeeds. :white_check_mark:

jon: I'll post results in this thread when replay finishes. For visibility, tagging SRE: @sam @maya

maya: quick note — consider also measuring per-model kv_miss variance. Some models show higher miss sensitivity. If we detect high variance, we should pin model->kernel mapping more aggressively.

rekha: good point. let's collect model-level kv_miss stats during the canary. I'll add to the replay dashboard.

jon: ok starting replay now. will update.
